- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and price is trending up, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.  
- After a sharp spike in true price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overestimates continuation — cap forecast growth to 5–7% max for next 3–5 days.  
- If true price shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often lags — adjust forecast to match recent downward trend.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early days of a 30-day forecast — apply a 2–3% upward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative — increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to reflect low volatility bias.
